prompt: Write a method that checks whether the parentheses in a string are balanced. Complete the isBalanced method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: A single integer counter is enough to check one kind of bracket: it records the current nesting depth. Going negative means a ')' appeared with nothing open -- which is why ")(" is unbalanced even though it has equal counts -- and a nonzero final value means some '(' was never closed. Returning false immediately on a negative depth catches that case at the exact character where it happens.
hints: Keep an int depth starting at 0: add 1 on '(' and subtract 1 on ')', ignoring every other character.
If depth ever becomes negative, you can return false immediately -- a ')' had no matching '('.
After the loop, the string is balanced only if depth is exactly 0.
